newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela doesn't plan dollar bank accounts.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela doesn't plan dollar bank accounts.

text.p: Venezuelan authorities do not plan to allow local banks to open dollar-denominated savings accounts and are investigating mutual funds that currently offer the service, Banking Superintendent Francisco Debera said.
"We're currently inspecting those that are attracting dollars to see if legally they can do so," Debera told Reuters in a telephone interview.
Debera said he did not expect the Banking Superintendency to modify current banking regulations to allow dollar-denominated local bank accounts.

But as some mutual funds currently offering dollar accounts "are not governed by banking laws, but rather capital markets laws, we'll shortly be meeting with the National Securities Commission to review the situation," he said.
Many Venezuelans saw their savings disappear in a 1994-5 banking crisis when a number of failing banks salted away funds in offshore dollar accounts.
Debera said he was wary of anything similar occurring in the future.
